title: icg status command with blind-spot self-report
description: One command printing current rule-pack version, last successful self-update check, and a hardcoded KNOWN_LIMITATIONS list (cloud-hosted Codex, absolute-path wrapper bypass, etc.). Operationalizes the plan's own 'don't oversell' principle live rather than leaving it as prose a human has to reread. Objection: only as honest as it's kept current -- risks becoming stale documentation with extra steps if not maintained. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #5 (merged #97+#72).

title: Poison-pill auto-rollback
description: If a fresh release's deny-rate spikes abnormally above a rolling baseline within the first M commands, auto-revert the self-update trust pointer to the prior release and log loudly. Closes a serious gap: a bad release silently degrading the whole fleet at once. Objection: the rollback trigger itself needs to be conservative -- could misfire on a legitimately bad day of command hygiene, not just a bad release. Depends on Phase 0's trust-pointer mechanism existing first. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #3.

title: Per-repo signed override
description: An overrides/<repo>.toml schema (which rule IDs are exempted, mandatory expiry date) routed through the same Layer 1/2 release-integrity CI gates as a rule-pack release -- a real escape hatch that doesn't undermine tamper-resistance, not a silent local bypass. Objection: overrides accumulate over time into Swiss-cheese coverage if not actively curated -- needs a forced re-justification cadence, mirroring Layer 1's staleness-flagging philosophy. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #7.

title: Stale-HEAD push guard
description: Before allowing git push, compare the local checkout's tracked remote HEAD against the actual current remote HEAD (live check); if they differ, fail the push and redirect the agent to pull and resolve first. Simpler revision of the original shared-tree-collision idea (cross-process /proc scanning), per user direction 2026-08-13. Catches a different failure mode than the documented git-index-race incident (that one was uncommitted work getting swept into another worker's commit within the SAME shared tree, before any push) -- this catches pushing on top of state that's since moved. Deliberate, scoped exception to the no-I/O-in-hot-path engine constraint: git push is already a network operation, so a live remote-HEAD check here doesn't set a precedent for adding I/O to other guarded commands. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #2 (revised mechanism).

title: ReDoS check on submitted rule packs
description: CI check in icg-ci flagging catastrophic-backtracking-prone regex patterns in a submitted pack before it ships, via a timeout-bounded fuzz check or a known ReDoS-pattern detector. Defends against an honest authoring mistake, not an adversarial attack -- squarely inside the stated threat model despite superficially sounding like security hardening. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #7.

title: Graduated fail-open to fail-closed policy for guard crashes
description: In the beginning, the guard dying (e.g. OOM-killed mid-check) does NOT halt the fleet -- fails open, matching org-rule-guard.py's existing philosophy. As the guard's reliability is validated over time, shift to a fail-closed posture where the fleet can't run without the guard being healthy. Graduation signal ties to the poison-pill auto-rollback mechanism (icg-2ck) already tracking per-release deny-rate health -- e.g. N consecutive releases with zero poison-pill triggers -- rather than inventing a new maturity signal from scratch; exact threshold TBD at implementation time. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #6 (policy per user direction 2026-08-13).

title: Per-rule enable/disable feature flag
description: Revised from the original fleet-wide single-rule kill-switch design per user direction 2026-08-13: implement as a feature flag on each guarded_pattern (enabled: true/false), part of normal rule-pack data, toggled through the SAME release-integrity pipeline (Layer 1/2) as any other rule-pack change -- simpler, reuses existing infrastructure, no separate trust-pointer axis. Tradeoff to keep visible: this means disabling a misbehaving rule takes exactly as long as a normal release, which does NOT satisfy the original motivation (stop an actively-harmful rule before the next full release cycle completes). If genuine emergency-speed single-rule disable is ever needed, that's a distinct, unresolved requirement -- not solved by this bead. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #8 (revised).

title: Guard CI/build pods on iad-ci
description: Extend coverage to Argo Workflow pods, including this project's own icg-ci release pipeline, not just interactive Claude Code/Codex sessions. First step: wire the PATH-wrapper into the shared Argo Workflow executor image. Strongest justification is self-referential -- the release pipeline that guards everything else should itself be guarded. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #1.

title: Install-time smoke test vs org-rule-guard.py
description: Send one known org-rule-guard.py-covered case (e.g. a .github/workflows/ write attempt) through and confirm exactly one system reports the denial, not both redundantly or neither -- confirms no conflict/confusing duplication between the two guards. Framing per user direction 2026-08-13: this is an interim step, not a permanent coexistence check -- org-rule-guard.py is expected to eventually be deprecated once this project's coverage supersedes it (see plan.md Overview, revised). Only proves the one tested case, not broader overlap elsewhere. From /plan-idea-gen run 2 (2026-08-13), docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #10.

title: Practice/dry-run mode
description: A --practice flag routing all deny verdicts through additionalContext instead of blocking, for onboarding trust-building. HARD REQUIREMENT from the kill pass: a persistent, impossible-to-miss banner printed on every guarded check while active (not just at startup), or an operator could forget to ever flip it to enforcing and believe they're protected when they aren't. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #8.

title: Docker destructive-ops pack
description: New rule pack (packs/docker.*) covering docker system prune -a, docker volume rm, and forced removal of tagged/in-use images -- same Pack/GuardedPattern shape as the existing Vault pack. Cleanest coverage-breadth expansion found in the whole ideation pool, zero new architecture needed. Objection: real but bounded uncertainty about how much direct Docker-CLI exposure exists in this environment versus everything already routing through Argo Workflows. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #9 (gap round G1).

title: Canary rollout via NEEDLE --identifier
description: Add a canary release channel alongside stable in the self-updater's trust pointer; launch one NEEDLE worker with --identifier canary-icg tracking it before promoting a release fleet-wide. Concrete implementation of Layer 4's deferred staged-rollout, using infrastructure that already exists for free. Objection: one canary instance may not generate enough command diversity to be meaningful alone -- it's a backstop behind CI, not the primary verification. Depends on Phase 0's trust-pointer mechanism. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #4.

title: Pack-authoring scaffold tool (icg new-pack)
description: A CLI subcommand generating a new rule-pack file with the required Pack/GuardedPattern fields pre-filled, plus a paired regression-test stub. Structurally enforces the Layer-1 'every rule needs a test' discipline instead of relying on an author remembering. Objection: may be premature at only ~9 planned packs; payoff scales with pack count. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #2.

title: Auto-denial-becomes-test
description: Every deny verdict automatically appends its command as a new regression-suite case (hook a --record-as-test path into the deny-dispatch code, writing to tests/regression/<pack-id>.cases). Requires periodic curation/pruning so the suite doesn't grow unbounded and slow CI -- do not make it permanently automatic without a pruning step. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #1.

title: Codex hook-version compatibility matrix
description: Add a matrix stage to icg-ci running the Codex hook adapter's test suite against the last 3 minor Codex CLI releases (pinned versions), failing the build on regression. Codex's PreToolUse hook is confirmed still churning (~5 months old, scope still expanding per docs/notes/multi-harness-integration.md) -- this catches breakage from Codex's own upstream changes before it silently degrades that front-end's coverage. Objection: only pays for itself while Codex's hook API keeps churning -- could become dead CI weight once it stabilizes. From /plan-idea-gen run 2026-08-13, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md, finalist #6 (gap round G4).
